repair_quotes.exact_quote:
**Repair principle (smallest):** make the recovery path re-establish the same durability invariant the insert path guarantees — *a writing segment that holds un-persisted, WAL-derived documents must have a live `wal_file_` with `has_record()==true`*. Concretely, at the end of `SegmentImpl::recover()` (segment.cc:4193-4301), when records were replayed, (re)open the segment's own `wal_file_` against the existing WAL in append mode (the existing `open_wal_file()` already opens non-`create_new` when the file exists, 4303-4322) instead of leaving it null. Then `flush()`'s guard (2220-2222) correctly sees un-persisted data, and `dump()`/`switch_to_new_segment_for_writing()` will persist the forward block (`finish_memory_components` → `add_persisted_block`) and commit it (`update_version`) before the WAL is removed and the segment is promoted.

The alternative — changing the `flush()` guard to key off "does this segment hold un-persisted data" rather than `wal_file_` — is a larger blast-radius change; the recover-side fix is the minimal one that restores the intended lifecycle (recovered data behaves exactly like freshly inserted data w.r.t. flush/dump/optimize). Either way, the invariant to enforce is: **`switch_to_new_segment_for_writing()` must not promote a writing segment whose forward data has not actually been persisted.**

An explicit `dirty_after_recovery_` flag consulted by the same gate is an equivalent variant. Fixing it at this one site also repairs the identical window in `Flush()`/`Close()` (currently silent no-ops after recovery) and in every DDL path that funnels through `switch_to_new_segment_for_writing` / `commit_schema_change_with_new_writing_segment` (`CreateIndex`/`DropIndex`/`AddColumn`/`DropColumn`/`AlterColumn`, `collection.cc:501-503, 674-676, 1154-1156, 1226-1228, 1310-1312`). Either way, the invariant to enforce is: **`switch_to_new_segment_for_writing()` must not promote a writing segment whose forward data has not actually been persisted.**

So after any insert, the writing segment holds: RAM state (`doc_ids_`, `memory_store_`, memory indexers, in-memory writing-block counters — `internal_insert`, `segment.cc:837-881`) **plus a live `wal_file_` handle whose `has_record()` is true** (`src/db/index/storage/wal/local_wal_file.h:75-77`: file size > header).

**Recovery** — `CollectionImpl::recovery()` (`src/db/collection.cc:1836-1892`) opens the writing segment; `SegmentImpl::Open` sees a `writing_forward_block` in the meta and calls `recover()` (`segment.cc:490-501`). `recover()` (`segment.cc:4193-4301`) opens the WAL into a **local** `recover_wal_file` that is closed on scope exit (`segment.cc:4206-4215`), and replays each record by calling `internal_insert/internal_update/internal_upsert/internal_delete` **directly** (`segment.cc:4250-4266`) — bypassing `append_wal`. 

So after recovery the RAM state is identical to the insert case (which is why reads work): `doc_count()` is `doc_ids_.size()` (`segment.cc:589-600`), `fetch` serves rows from `memory_store_` while `has_writing_forward_block()` (`segment.cc:2743-2757`), and `scan` unions persisted blocks with the memory store (`segment.cc:2825-2841`). **The one differing piece of state is the member `wal_file_`, which stays `nullptr`** even though the on-disk WAL holds every recovered doc. The invariant flush depends on — “`wal_file_ == nullptr` ⟺ nothing unpersisted” (a full flush removes the WAL and resets the handle, `segment.cc:2304-2315`) — is broken exactly in this window. Note the version file on disk is also stale (last written pre-crash; `update_version` runs only inside a full flush, `segment.cc:2300-2302, 4414-4426`), so the WAL is the *only* durable copy of the docs.

Nothing persists: no `memory_store_->flush()` (2233-2236), no indexer flushes (2238-2264), no `finish_memory_components()` (2288-2298 → 4342-4411, the step that converts the writing block into persisted block metas and demotes memory indexers to persisted ones), no `update_version()` (2300-2302), no WAL removal (2304-2315). `dump()` then seals and returns OK.
